xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The communication is a GST Audit Report (Form GST ADT-02) issued under Section 65(6) of the CGST/KGST Act for the financial year 2022–23, proposing a total tax and interest liability of approximately ₹1.63 crore on account of alleged differences in turnover between GSTR-3B V/s Books, Excess claim of ITC - claimed in GSTR-3B but not reflecting in GSTR-2A/8A, Excess claim of ITC - claimed in GSTR-3B but Short in GSTR-2A/8A, ITC difference in Books V/s GSTR-3B, Interest for belated payment on Trade Payables, Belated reversal of Ineligible ITC through DRC – 03, Ineligible ITC Claimed, ITC reversal for non-filing of Form ITC -04,
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: No specific penalty, restriction, or sanction has been imposed pursuant to the communication at this stage. The audit report recommendation raised vide Form GST ADT-02 comprises tax and interest liabilities only
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The matter relates to Stanley OEM Sofas Limited wholly owned subsidiary of the listed entity. The liability remains provisional at this stage, pending the company's review and determination of response. Any confirmed liability, if crystallized pursuant to further proceedings or payment, may have a financial impact to that extent.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Bengaluru
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The matter pertains to a Show Cause Notice issued by the Office of the Deputy Commissioner of Commercial Taxes (Audit)-4.1, Bengaluru, under Section 73 of the KGST Act, 2017, against Stanley OEM Sofas Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Stanley Lifestyles Limited. The notice relates to alleged short declaration of turnover and non-reversal of Input Tax Credit on creditors outstanding beyond 180 days for the tax period April 2021 to March 2022.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The expected financial implication is ₹55.63 lakh towards tax and interest. No penalty has been imposed at this stage. The matter is currently under consideration, and the subsidiary is evaluating appropriate representations.The quantum of claim, as stated in the Show Cause Notice dated 09th July 2025, is ₹55.63 lakh comprising tax of ₹2.74 lakh and interest of ₹52.89 lakh under the KGST/CGST Act, 2017

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: A Show Cause Notice was received from Registrar of Companies Bangalore, Ministry of Corporate Affairs against Directors and Ex-Director of Sana Lifestyles Limited alleging non-compliance with Sections 188 r/w 184 of the Companies Act, 2013 for related party transactions during FY 2018-19, undertaken without fresh/omnibus Board approvals. xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: Notice from the office of the Superintendent of Central Tax, Bengaluru South Commissionerate, directing the Company to explain the mismatch in ITC within 7 working days, reverse the ineligible ITC of ₹1,59,37,182.67 with interest via Form DRC-03, or submit documentary evidence if contesting the computation.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The Company has received a notice from the Office of the Superintendent of Central Tax, Bengaluru South Commissionerate citing a mismatch in Input Tax Credit (ITC) between GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B for FY 2022–23 amounting to ₹1,59,37,182.67. The Company has been asked to provide its explanation within 7 working days and reverse the ineligible ITC, if applicable or submit documentary evidence if contesting the computation. The matter is being examined and necessary action will be taken in due course.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: Owing to the mismatch in Input Tax Credit (ITC) between GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B for FY 2022–23 amounting to ₹1,59,37,182.67 which is liable to be recovered along with interest under Section 50(1) of the CGST Act, 2017, from the date of wrongful availment till the date of payment.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Regional Director South East Region, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Hyderabad
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The Regional Director has passed an order against Stanley OEM Sofas Limited, Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company, under Section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013, imposing monetary penalties on the following officers in default for contravention relating to entering into related party transactions without requisite approval: • Mrs. Shubha Sunil (Director) – ₹5,00,000/– • Mr. Sunil Suresh (Director) – ₹5,00,000/– Total Penalty: ₹10,00,000/– Further, Mr. Ananthakrishnan Viswanath (Ex Director), appointed as a Non-Executive Director on 30.12.2015 and who ceased from the Board on 20.03.2024, was not involved in the day-to-day management of the Company and was not aware of any related party transactions that had taken place. Accordingly, the penalty levied on Mr. Ananthakrishnan Viswanath was set aside.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The Company had entered into related party transactions without obtaining the prior approval of the Board/Shareholders, thereby contravening Section 188 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the applicable rules thereunder
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: There is no material impact on the financial, operational or other activities of the Company on account of this order. The financial impact is limited to the penalties imposed on the officers in default as detailed in coloumn 2.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Regional Director South East Region, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Hyderabad
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The Regional Director has passed an order against Stanley OEM Sofas Limited, Wholly Owned Subsidiary of the Company, under Section 405 of the Companies Act, 2013, imposing monetary penalties on the following officers in default for contravention relating to provisioning interest on outstanding amount to MSME vendors in the financials: • Company ₹40,000/ *Mrs. Shubha Sunil (Director) – ₹40,000/– • Mr. Sunil Suresh (Director) – ₹40,000/ Total Penalty: ₹1,20,000/– Further, Mr. Ananthakrishnan Viswanath (Ex Director), appointed as a Non-Executive Director on 30.12.2015 and who ceased from the Board on 20.03.2024, was not involved in the day-to-day management of the Company and was not aware of the fact. Accordingly, the penalty levied on Mr. Ananthakrishnan Viswanath was set aside.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The company has not provided the interest on outstanding amount to MSME vendors in its financials.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: There is no material impact on the financial, operational or other activities of the Company on account of this order. The financial impact is limited to the penalties imposed on the company and the officers in default as detailed in Coloumn 2.
